about_the_game:
SYNOPSIS

Night Shift: 1999 is an upcoming 1-bit visual novel where you play as Isra Bayassee, a centuries aged vampire, as she struggles to reintegrate into society. As a player-driven narrative tale, your choices will shape the story's outcomes. With five routes and eleven different endings, each playthrough will grant new rewards.

Balance work, vampirism, and socialising as you explore Kings Cross during the last year of the millennium. Keep a lid on your darkest desires and be rewarded with a deeper understanding of what it means to live again.

Or don’t — no one will stop you. You’re a vampire, after all.

Meet a cast of intriguing individuals all running from secrets of their own as you try to run from yours. The past will catch up eventually but what that means, you decide.

Experience heartbreak and betrayal — and maybe love, if you try hard enough — as you work the night shift at the local hospital. Everyone has a story of their own, and it's up to you to find that out.

After all, who wants to celebrate New Year's alone?

Find new ways to satiate your hunger that won't lead to a forced resignation — or a stake through the heart. As you come across a variety of blood bags, not all of them will be so forgiving.

Will you blend into the backdrop of humanity or push against the fold? It's up to you to choose what kind of person you want to be — or if you want to be a humane at all.

The consequences of your actions will always be close behind.

FEATURES:

  • Five characters of various origins to discover

  • Multiple endings per character

  • Stylised 1-bit pixel art

  • LGBT+ characters and topics handled with care (and plenty of humour)

  • Migratory loss and community building... but make it Supernatural(TM)

  • One secret route

  • ... and in-game collectables!

Born and died in the sixteenth century, Isra has taken on many names and faces to survive this everchanging world. Discover her colourful past as you discover the world around you. 

Now finding herself starting anew in Kings Cross, she must navigate her condition, her relationships and most importantly, her menial job to see the start of the twenty-first century. But the past has a funny way of catching up to you, and landlords don't care if you're dead or not — they only want the rent when it's due.

Some of us aren’t lucky enough to come back to life — we just stay dead.

Having met her end on one night in the roaring 20’s, Alma decided to stick around for one last dance. Although she’s got enough unfinished business to fill not one, but two closets with skeletons, she insists haunting the living is her choice. It’s up to Isra to get to the bottom of all that though.

Or not. It's up to you in the end.

Be careful — she bites. 

Being a werewolf is a fulltime job for Aleks. Although she only transforms once a month, she likes the aesthetic so much she can't seem to put the claws and fangs away. No one can say for sure what she does during the daytime but once the sun sets, you're sure to find her prowling the streets. 

Enemies to lovers or enemies til the end? Isra's not quite sure but you might be.

Some might say Soonee is a fish out of water, but she prefers to say she's merely getting her sea legs. 

Having lost her pod during their yearly move, she's found herself being the sole occupier of Elizabeth Bay year-round. Although she's not keen on staying for long, something keeps bringing her back to shallow waters — and away from her family. 

Isra didn't expect to add "detective" to her resume, but only you can make that choice.

Overworked and overstressed — caffeine is the only superpower he has. 

Isaac has an impeccable bedside manner but an atrocious work-life balance. He keeps insisting it's fine if he picks up that extra shift, but how much more can one man do? And why does he keep doing it? There's no photos in his wallet that might point to a clue and — hey, how did you get his wallet in the first place?

The least Isra can do is buy him another coffee while they're both on their break, but maybe you'll be the one to do a pulse check on his life outside of the hospital.

content_descriptors.notes: This game contains mature language, and has mentions and references to death and alcohol. Viewer discretion is advised.
